newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends off on bearish oil data forecasts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends off on bearish oil data forecasts.

text.p: NYMEX crude reversed early session gains to end lower Tuesday on expectations that weekly oil inventory data will show a bearish build in crude stocks, traders said.
"We were overbought earlier in the session, and if we get a build in crude stocks, we are bound to go lower again at the open tomorrow," said James Cordier, trader with Allendale Inc in Florida.
May crude ended seven cents a barrel lower at $19.83 after rising as high as $20.09. May gasoline ended 0.06 cent a gallon lower at 61.90 cents.

Traders expected crude stocks to rise by up to 3.5 million barrels in the American Petroleum Institute's (API) weekly report Tuesday evening due to a continued strong pace of imports. The data reflects the week ended April 11.
When the API report was released after the market's close, it said crude stocks rose by 2.97 million barrels. This was the sixth consecutive weekly crude stock build.

Unseasonably cold weather in the U.S. Northeast was expected to have increased demand, so distillate stocks, which include heating oil and diesel, were expected by traders to fall. May heat oil ended up 0.18 cent a gallon at 54.85 cents.
However, the API said distillate stocks grew 2.59 million barrels.
The API also defied expectations with gasoline stocks.

Traders had expected a tempered gasoline stock draw of about one million barrels as implied demand was seen easing somewhat from the 8.3 million barrel per day level in last week's data, which many thought was overstated.
Indeed, implied demand dropped and the API said gasoline stocks grew a surprising 3.63 million barrels.
